tier_reason: The README Notes section names GNU as and the clang assembler but gives only a qualitative sentence ('performance is often better than gnu as and much better than the clang assembler') with no numbers, workload, machine or flags. The repo has no benchmark code: test/test.sh only checks minias's .text bytes against clang's encoding for correctness and times nothing.

corrections.caveats: Only evidence is one README sentence with no numbers, versions, machine or workload; the repo has no benchmark script (test/test.sh is an encoding-correctness test that uses clang as the reference). The author ranks speed third among goals (simple, tiny, fast) and says performance is limited by the generated parser; the parser generator was swapped (PackCC, then vendored Minipeg) in May 2026 and the speed sentence was last edited in that commit, so any measurement behind it is unpublished. Roadmap items still open: simple immediate expressions, self-hosting with chibicc, and testing every opcode with all variants. Hobby project ('written for fun and learning'), 231 stars, not widely referenced.

notes: Metadata checks out: ISC licence (LICENSE file), 231 stars, 16 forks, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-06-24 ('Clarify assembly capabilities and remove contact info'), so active and copyable. Kept at tier D as a directional claim against GNU as and the clang integrated assembler; shortcomings: no numbers or benchmark code anywhere, low notability (<1k stars), unfinished opcode coverage.
